description: We are THE NEXT HORIZON, a passionate team focused on the "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" challenge. Our crew—Muharrem, Elif, Deniz, Ada U., Batuhan, and Ada O.—excels in coding, 3D design, and creative problem-solving. Our goal is to transform complex space data into an interactive Mars survival guide. We thrive on STEM and innovation. Let's map the future of space exploration together!
summary:
We are a team committed to contributing to humanity's journey to Mars through scientific research and technological design.
As part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we are developing a comprehensive map that explores Mars's remarkable regions and aims to guide future space missions.
In our project, we aim to identify important geographical formations, surface features, scientifically significant areas, and potential landing sites on Mars. We evaluate these locations based on criteria such as surface structure, environmental conditions, terrain characteristics, and exploration potential.
Our team uses scientific data provided by NASA to better understand different regions of Mars and transform this information into a visual, accessible, and interactive map.
Our goal is not simply to illustrate the geography of Mars, but to identify important exploration areas, potential landing sites, and safe exploration routes for astronauts and research teams who may travel to Mars in the future.
We see Mars as much more than a planetary map; we are charting the exploration routes of the future through science!🚀
details:
THE NEXT HORIZON – PROJECT DESCRIPTION

1. What does your project do, and how does it work?

The Interplanetary Survival Guide: Mars Map is an interactive and educational mapping project that aims to provide information for future crewed missions to Mars by exploring the planet’s geographical features, surface formations, and environmental conditions.

Our project introduces different regions of Mars by drawing on NASA’s open scientific datasets, images obtained from Mars orbiters, and scientific research. Through the map, users can explore the planet’s major geographical features and learn about mountains, craters, valleys, plains, and other geological formations.

In addition, we aim to assess factors that may be important for future exploration missions, such as regional temperature conditions, the potential presence of water ice, surface characteristics, and environmental conditions. In this way, users will not only become visually familiar with Mars but will also gain a deeper understanding of the planet through scientific data.

2. What are the benefits of your project?

Our project aims to make space exploration more understandable and accessible to everyone.

  • It makes learning about the geographical and geological features of Mars easier.
  • It supports the use of NASA’s open-access data in education and scientific research.
  • It highlights environmental factors that may be important for future Mars exploration missions.
  • It helps students develop scientific data literacy, interpretation, and research skills.
  • It raises curiosity and awareness about space science and planetary exploration.
  • It supports interdisciplinary learning by bringing together geography, astronomy, science, and technology.

3. What is the intended impact of your project?

The main goal of our project is to evaluate Mars’s potential significance for humanity in the future through scientific data and to raise awareness of interplanetary exploration.

Understanding the planet’s surface conditions, natural resources, and environmental challenges is essential for making informed decisions about life on Mars and future crewed missions. We aim for our map to bring this information together on a single platform and support users in developing scientific thinking and evaluation skills.

In the long term, we want our project to become more than just an introductory map of Mars. We envision it as an educational exploration guide that inspires future space research.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

During the development of our project, we used NASA’s publicly available scientific data sources, images from Mars exploration missions, and AI-powered digital tools. We explored Mars’s geographical structure, topographical features, surface formations, and exploration routes, integrating scientific information into our project.

The data sources and digital tools we used are listed below:

Scientific Data Sources:

1. NASA Mars Trek – Aerial Views of Mars

NASA Mars Trek

We used this resource to examine Mars from a bird’s-eye perspective, explore different regions of the planet, and obtain visual references for our mapping work.

2. USGS Astrogeology – Mars Topographic Maps

USGS Astrogeology

We used this resource to examine elevation differences, surface formations, and topographical features on Mars, supporting our geographical assessments.

3. NASA Science – Curiosity’s Proposed Path

Curiosity’s Proposed Path

By examining the Curiosity rover’s route around Mount Sharp, we gathered information about Martian rock formations, craters, surface characteristics, and exploration routes.

4. NASA Mars 2020 Mission – Raw Images

NASA Mars 2020 Raw Images

We examined raw images and camera information captured by the Perseverance rover on the surface of Mars, making use of authentic visual data from the planet.

AI & Digital Design Tools:

1. Antigravity (User Interface and General Project Design) We utilized Antigravity to build the foundational digital architecture of our project. The User Interface (UI) of our platform and all other structural design components were designed end-to-end on Antigravity, ensuring complete visual consistency and a seamless user experience.

2. Anthropic Claude (Simulation Game Development) To enhance the interactive nature of our platform, we integrated two distinct simulation games. We used Claude extensively to design the game mechanics, logical flow, and the overall game design structure for both simulations.

3. Google Gemini (Asset Generation and Translation Verification) We utilized Gemini as a dual-purpose visual and textual assistant. It was instrumental in generating AI-based visual assets for the project. Additionally, we used Gemini to identify English/Turkish translation errors and verify the accuracy of our bilingual texts.

4. OpenAI ChatGPT (Content Proofreading and Prompt Engineering) ChatGPT was used for the final proofreading of our project documentation. We utilized it to correct grammatical errors, refine our sentence structures, and polish our translations into fluent English. It also assisted in optimizing the prompt engineering process to generate high-quality visual concepts alongside Gemini.

5. Canva (Team Poster and Visual Composition) We used Canva's design suite to assemble, edit, and organize the raw AI-generated images produced by Gemini and ChatGPT. Canva was our primary tool for designing the NEXT HORIZON team poster and finalizing all visual presentation materials for the project.

We designed a strategic workflow where each AI tool served a specific, specialized purpose. We built our UI and overall design using Antigravity, developed the mechanics of our two simulation games with Claude, perfected our texts and translations using Gemini and ChatGPT, and brought all our AI-generated visuals together in Canva to create "THE NEXT HORIZON" team identity.

Overall Evaluation

By combining these tools, we brought NASA’s authentic scientific data together with visual design and AI-assisted content development. This allowed us to explore Mars’s geographical features not only through theoretical knowledge but also through data obtained from real space exploration missions.

Authentic scientific data forms the foundation of our project, while AI and digital design tools help us interpret, organize, and present this information more effectively to users. 🚀

5. How creative and innovative is your project?

The creative aspect of our project lies in combining the scientific exploration of Mars with the idea of a future-oriented exploration and survival guide.

While many existing resources introduce the general characteristics of the planet, we aim to develop an approach that evaluates different geographical regions of Mars in terms of their potential relevance to future crewed missions.

What makes our project different is that we approach the Mars map not merely as a tool for displaying locations, but as an exploration platform supported by scientific data.

As users explore different regions of Mars, we want them to think about questions such as:

  • Which regions might be more suitable for future research missions?
  • Which areas of Mars may have the potential to contain water ice?
  • How might the planet’s surface formations affect the movement of exploration rovers?
  • What challenges could temperature variations and environmental conditions create for crewed missions?
  • If a research base were to be established on Mars in the future, which scientific criteria should be considered?

Through these questions, we bring scientific research together with problem-solving and exploration.

6. What factors did your team consider?

While developing our project, we considered key factors such as scientific accuracy, data reliability, user experience, and the needs of future space missions.

In particular, we focused on:

  • Scientific Reliability: Using data obtained from NASA and other trustworthy scientific sources.
  • Geographical Features: Evaluating Mars’s mountains, craters, valleys, plains, and surface formations.
  • Environmental Conditions: Taking temperature variations, atmospheric conditions, radiation, and surface characteristics into account.
  • Natural Resources: Investigating the potential presence of water ice and other natural resources that may be useful in the future.
  • Future Missions: Assessing the challenges and requirements that may arise during future crewed missions to Mars.
  • User Experience: Ensuring that the map is designed to be easy to understand and use for people of different age groups.
  • Teamwork: Bringing together research, data analysis, content development, writing, and design processes according to each team member’s strengths and abilities.

Our Project’s Overall Vision

As The Next Horizon, we see Mars not merely as a planet observed from a distance, but as a new world that could open the door to future exploration through scientific research.

With this project, we aim to transform the scientific data provided by NASA into a meaningful product, make space exploration more accessible, and help young people develop their scientific thinking skills.

For us, every coordinate is a new discovery, every piece of scientific data is a new clue, and every research effort is a step toward humanity’s future.

THE NEXT HORIZON – Beyond Earth, Towards the Future! 🚀
